summary: Iteration 17 backend testing verifying /api/notifications (type=order) and /api/pos/online-orders return consistent order IDs (zero divergence). Root cause of user-reported bug was a frontend polling bug (already fixed by E1); backend was and remains correct. Wrote 7 new alignment tests; all pass. Full sequential regression across iter10+iter11+iter12+iter13+iter15+iter16+iter17 = 83 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1002 /notifications includes SelfOrder.status IN ['pending', 'Pesanan Diterima'] whereas /pos/online-orders (line 1638) uses ['Pesanan Diterima', 'Menunggu kasir', 'Menunggu konfirmasi'] — the sets do NOT match. If any future self-order is written with status 'pending', it would appear in notif but NOT in POS modal, reproducing the exact user bug at the data layer. Recommend unifying both queries via a shared constant like PENDING_SELF_ORDER_STATUSES.
server.py:1093-1146 /self-order sets status='Pesanan Diterima' consistently, so today the two endpoints DO align in practice, but the divergent status lists are a latent risk.
server.py file is 2115 lines — should be split into routers (still applies from iter16 review).

New self-orders default to 'Pesanan Diterima' and appear in both endpoints within 1s. Accept transitions status to 'paid' which correctly removes it from POS queue. rca of the issue: User bug 'Notification says new order, POS modal says 0 antrean' was NOT a backend divergence bug. Backend endpoints /api/notifications (type=order) and /api/pos/online-orders return identical order IDs for pending self-orders in scope (verified by iter17). Root cause was a frontend polling bug: a premature `return` inside a useEffect prevented the reloadOnlineOrders setInterval from ever starting, so the modal state stayed at its initial empty array even though the notification bell was polled independently. E1 fixed frontend (App.js:128-175); backend needed no change. Iter17 codifies the alignment contract to prevent future regressions.
